beats.text: What if your perfect match is a lie?
OkCupid took pairs who were a bad match, just thirty percent, and told them they were ninety.
They messaged more. And they acted like a good match, even though they weren't.
The site's own verdict: the myth of compatibility works just as well as the truth.
When OkCupid admitted it in twenty fourteen, users were furious.
So maybe chemistry is partly what you're told to expect.

sources: OkCupid (2014), 'We Experiment On Human Beings!' (Christian Rudder). Pairs with actual 30% match shown 90%: more first messages, acted as if good match; quote 'the mere myth of compatibility works just as well as the truth'. Backlash after disclosure, July 2014.
